Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the Authority Members are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each
month, closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general
business session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Authority Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

 GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the Housing Authority are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular
City Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City
Clerk's Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at
https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers first. After all speakers in the Chambers have spoken,
the Presiding Officer will call upon those participating via zoom or teleconference.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the Housing Authority as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, virtually, email, phone call, mail and any other method which may become
available. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such times when a State of
Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the Housing Authority, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the Housing Authority meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the Housing
Authority if any agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items
to be continued, the Housing Authority can direct the item be placed on the next Housing Authority
agenda or the current meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be
reconvened as an Adjourned Regular Meeting of the Housing Authority and action upon the published
agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular Housing Authority meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a
Housing Authority meeting. There are times when the housing Authority receives written material,
revised material after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be
available for public view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials

  4
 and any other public document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California
Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
Housing Authority Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the
Housing Authority Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility.
For further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

  Council/Authority  Member  Maria  Davila,  Council/Authority  Member  Gil
  Hurtado;  City  Treasurer  Jose De La Paz, City  Manager/Executive  Director
  Rob  Houston,  City  Attorney/Authority  Counsel  Raul  F. Salinas

LATE  Council/Authority  Member  Maria  del Pilar  Avalos

DEVELOPMIENT  It is recommended  that the City  Council  and Housing  Authority:

  a.  Approve  the Memorandum  of Understanding  (MOU)  among  the City
  of South  Gate  (Contract  No.  2026-33-CC),  the South  Gate Housing
  Authority  (Contract  No.  2026-01-HA),  and Habitat  for Humanity  of
  Greater  Los Angeles  or Partnership  Housing,  Inc.  (Developer)  to
  establish  initial  terms  for negotiating  a Disposition,  Development  and
  Loan  Agreement  (DDA)  and an Affordable  Housing  and Loan
  Agreement  (AHA);  and

  b.  Authorize  the Chairperson  of the South  Gate Housing  Authority  and
  Mayor  or authorized  designee  to execute  the MOU  in a fortn  approved
  by the City  Attorney.

  Carol  Averell,  Housing  Manager,  gave  the presentation.

  Council/Authority  MemberAvalos  asked  whether  staff  will  be presenting
  a detailed  financial  analysis  before  any binding  agreements  with  Habitat
  are considered  or executed.

  Ms. Averell  replied  in the affirmative  and stated  that the city  is already  in
  the process  of developing  the Disposition  and Development  Agreement.
  She explained  that the agreement  will  be presented  to the Council  and
  Housing  Authority  at a later  date, along  with  an item  regarding  the
  allocation  of any City  funding  for this project.  She noted  that  such  an
  allocation  is required  in order  for Habitat  to work  with  the city  and
  provide  a pro fori'na  and analysis  of the financing  and all funding  sources
  that will  be included  in the project.

  Council/Authority  Member  Avalos  stated that under  Security  and
  Covenants,  it indicates  that if a buyer  decides  to sell before  the 45-year
  period  is over, they must first offer the property  directly  to the developer.

  Ms. Averell  explained  that tl'iis requirement  is part of Habitat  for
  Humanity's  program.  Habitat  holds the first right  of rescission,  meaning
  that if a homeowner  chooses  to sell, the developer  has the right  to take
  back the property  and then select another  qualified  low-income  family  to
  purchase  it.

  Council/Authority  Member  Avalos  asked whether  the developer  would
  purchase  the property  at market  value or at the original  price  at which  it
  was initially  sold.

  Patrick  Sunpanich,  Senior  Director  for GovernmentAffairs  with  Habitat
  for Humanity,  responded  that the property  would  be purchased  at the
  market  rate at that time.

  Council/Authority  Member  Avalos  asked about the South Gate loan.

  Ms. Averell  responded  by outlining  the various  funding  sources  the city
  has applied  for in coru'iection  with  this project.  She explained  that the City
  has allocated  HOME  funds  specifically  for this development.  In addition,
  the City has secured  state funding,  designated  PHA  funds  for the project,
  and has applied  for CalHome  funding  to support  mortgage  assistance.

  Council/Authority  Member  Avalos  inquired  about the DTSC  grant funding
  that Habitat  has received  and the total amount  awarded.

  Naomi  Zahler,  Associate  Director  of Public  Funding  and Contracts  for
  Habitat,  stated that she believes  the DTSC  grant amount  is $800,000.

  Council/Authority  Member  Avalos  further  asked whether  there were any
  estimates  indicating  that remediation  costs might  exceed the DTSC  grant
  amount.

  Ms. Averell  believes  that pretty  much most of the money  is going  to be
  utilized  for that remediation.  The remediation  is quite  costly.  She also
  stated the city allocated  CDBG  funds for the demolition  of the structure.

  Council/Authority  Member  Avalos  asked what preliminary  risks or
  uncertainties  staff would  like the Council/Housing  Authority  to be aware
  of at this stage, if any.

  Mr. Perez stated that it will  be important  for the city to resume  remediation
  work,  including  demolition  of the building.  He emphasized  that no
  approvals  for the project  are being  considered  at this meeting.  Tlie project
  will  still  require  future  approval  by both the Planning  Coinrnission  and the
  City  Council.

  Council/Authority  Member  Avalos  asked whether  there was anything  in
  the proposed  MOU  that staff recommended  the Council  or Housing
  Authority  modify  prior  to approval,  or if staff was satisfied  with  the
  document  as presented.

  Mr. Perez stated that staff are satisfied  with  the MOU  as written  and
  recoinmends  moving  it forward  to the Plai'ming  Coinmission  and the City
  Council  for future  consideration.

  Council/Authority  Member  Avalos  asked if there were any external
  deadlines,  such as funding  cycles,  that could  affect  the project's
  completion  timeline.

  Ms. Averell  stated that for CDBG  funding,  the project  must be completed
  by the end of the year. She also noted that DTSC's  deadline  is tied to the
  completion  of the remediation  work.

  Vice Mayor/Vice  Chairperson  Rios asked how much  the City  and Habitat
  for Humanity  have spent to date and what the projected  total cost of the
  project  will  be.

  City  Manager/Executive  Director  Houston  clarified  for anyone  who may
  be new to the City's  housing-related  funding  discussions  over the past
  year that none of the 'Junding  for this project  comes  from  the General
  Fund.

  Ms. Averell  explained  that projects  of this type rely on multiple  'funding
  sources.

  Ms. Zahler  stated the spending  of about $200,000  of the DTSC  fund  so far.
  That's  just  for remediation  and doesn't  have the exact total for the
  remediation.  DTSC  has not expressed  concern  for the funding,  especially
  since DTSC  have waived  the fees on their  end. She also mentioned  that
  Habitat  for LA is exploring  a lot of funds  for the development,  including
  new market  tax credits  and LACAHSA  funds.

  Council/Authority  Member  Avalos  asked how much  additional  funding  the
  City  anticipates  contributing  to this specific  project,  excluding  General
  Fund dollars.

  Ms. Averell  responded  that tlie HOME  funds represent  the final  City-
  controlled  funding  source currently  coiui'nitted.  She explained  that the city
  must still  evaluate  all other funding  sources that Habitat  for Humanity  will
  bring  to the project.  This  evaluation  will  be part of the financial  analysis
  conducted  through  the pro fon'na to deteri'nine  tlie City's  total contribution.
  As an example,  she noted that the city applied  for $5 million  in CalHome
  funding  to support  mortgage  assistance  for two affordable  housing
  projects,  and the full  amount  was awarded.  Habitat  will  utilize  at least half
  of those funds to provide  up to $200,000  in mortgage  assistance  for the
  fourteen  (14) units.

  Council/Authority  Member  Hurtado  and Mayor/Chairperson  Barron
  expressed  that they are looking  forward  to seeing this project  get off the
  ground.

  City Attorney/Authority  Counsel  Salinas  reiterated  that he previously
  served on the Board  of Directors  for Habitat  for Humanity  of Greater  Los
  Angeles,  a role he was proud  to hold.  He clarified  that he no longer  serves
  on the fiduciary  board  and currently  participates  only  as a member  of the
  Ameritas  Board.  He further  stated that he has no legal obligations  to the
  organization  and does not receive  any income  from  it.

  Council/Authority  Member  Hurtado  stated that when the property  is
  eventually  sold, there will  be a profit  because  the original  appraisal  value
  is no longer  accurate.  He added that the proceeds  would  return  to the
  housing  program.

  Council/Authority  Member  Avalos  asked whether,  once all the properties
  are sold, the City  will  release the titles  to the new homeowners  indicating
  that the City-provided  mortgage  has been fully  paid off.

  Ms. Averell  clarified  that under  the mortgage  assistance  program,
  homeowners  will  still be responsible  for making  certain  mortgage
  payments.  She explained  that in some cases the City may structure  the
  assistance  as deferred,  meaning  repayment  would  occur upon sale,
  transfer,  or refinancing  of the property.  She added that the city is currently
